title: A finite tame cover has an etale model after a simultaneous finite root base change
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic a positive prime $p$, and let $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be a regular Noetherian separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in B$, with $r\geq0$, be such that $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ is a reduced strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and at every point $v\in V$ the $t_i$ vanishing at $v$ are part of a regular system of parameters of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. The closed subschemes $V(t_i)$ need not be irreducible or connected. Set $f=\prod_i t_i$ and $V^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$, with $f=1$ when $r=0$. Let $P\to V^\circ$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, writing $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] and $I(\bar v)=\{i:t_i(\bar v)=0\}$, its pullback to the punctured full root tower
$$\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(A[z_i:i\in I(\bar v)]/(z_i^m-t_i)_{i\in I(\bar v)}\bigr)[1/\prod_{i\in I(\bar v)}t_i]$$
is a finite disjoint union of copies of that tower. Transitions are the power maps for divisibility, and $m$ ranges over positive integers prime to $p$. Then there are a positive integer $n$ prime to $p$ and a finite etale morphism $Z\to V_n$, where
$$V_n=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i\bigr),$$
together with an isomorphism of $V_n^\circ=V_n\times_V V^\circ$-schemes
$$Z\times_{V_n}V_n^\circ\simeq P\times_{V^\circ}V_n^\circ.$$
No connectedness, Galois action, invertibility of $\deg P$, henselian hypothesis, residual-cover hypothesis, or choice of roots of unity is imposed. The empty cover and $r=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1(i)–(iii) and proof, printed pp.133–134: strict-local parameter-root quotient description and etale-local descent of the finite tame normalization; finite-type-over-a-field specialization. The simultaneous finite root level is the qc consequence of the local description, not a statement about infinite coefficient objects.
